texts: London's Attendant Cafe - Located in a converted 1920s underground Victorian public toilet in Fitzrovia, this shop serves specialty espresso from a marble urinal repurposed as the espresso machine base while original tiled walls and wrought-iron partitions create what may be the world's most atmospheric bathroom-turned-breakfast-spot.

Cafe Neizvestnny in St. Petersburg, Russia - Hidden inside a preserved 19th-century imperial carriage factory, this cafe occupies the original manager's office where Soviet cosmonauts once trained, serving coffee in vintage space-age cups while Sputnik-shaped pendants hang from ceilings still scarred by WWII shrapnel.

Sunrise Coffee in Cartagena, Colombia - Built into a restored 400-year-old colonial hacienda where coffee was once loaded onto ships bound for Spain, this shop features a living coffee tree growing through the center of its courtyard and serves cups roasted from beans grown in the surrounding hills using 18th-century Spanish filtration methods.
